title: Cardstock pack manifest (v0)
description: The declarative half of a card-pack. Anything this schema cannot express belongs in the pack's logic.js hooks — see CARD_PLATFORM_DESIGN.md §11. This schema is normative for the manifest format, and is ENFORCED: tools/pack-test.mjs validates every pack against it and tests/repo-gates.test.js gates the same check in CI. NOTE: logic.js itself is specified but NOT WIRED — no loader reads a pack's logic.js and no 'hook:' value is resolved anywhere in src/ (src/engine/movePipeline.js says so in its header). Every 'hook:<fn>' below is therefore a forward declaration, not a working escape hatch.

teams.description: This game is played in partnerships: seats are dealt round-robin into this many sides, so seat s plays for side s % teams and a partner sits `seats / teams` chairs away — opposite, at the four-seat two-side table this is for. One score per SIDE: a template still returns per-seat deltas and the engine folds them (src/engine/sides.js). Every seat count the pack offers must divide by it, or the pairing is not honest and the platform plays the pack as a free-for-all. Omit for a game where every seat plays for itself.

deck.description: Built-in deck id (standard-52, standard-54, standard-52x2) or relative path to a deck file, e.g. 'deck.json'. Built-in card ids follow '<suit>-<rank>' (clubs-2 … spades-A); built-in cards carry value:null — point values come from `scoring`.

rankLadder.description:
The pack's rank order, LOW TO HIGH ('3','4',…,'A','2' for Thirteen; '9','J','Q','K','10','A' for Pinochle). Resolved once per pack by src/engine/cards.js (`rankLadderOf`) and read from there by trick resolution and by the meld run window — no template reads this key itself. Omit it and the order is derived from the deck: numeric ranks ascending, then the ranks of the standard ladder (J Q K A), then anything else in deck order.

WHY IT LIVES HERE AND NOT IN `rules`: `rules` is refined per template by the four closed `$defs.rules-*` blocks below, so a key EVERY template shares would have to be repeated in all four and kept in step by hand. It is also not a template parameter — it is a fact about the deck, in the same class as `deck` itself, consumed by an engine primitive rather than by any one genre (the §13 extension policy's third step). Note the consequence: the `rules.*` gate in tests/repo-gates.test.js does not cover this key, so the honesty check for it is the unit tests in tests/rankLadder.test.js.

A rank the deck holds that this list does not name sits BELOW the whole ladder rather than above it — a card nobody gave a place to should not win a trick.

suitLadder.description: Optional suit order, LOW TO HIGH (Thirteen: spades, clubs, diamonds, hearts). The tiebreak that makes the order over the deck TOTAL, which a climbing game needs because 'play higher or pass' has no answer for a tie. Same placement rationale as `rankLadder` above. Read by `cardOrder` in src/engine/cards.js; no template consumes it yet.

tagline.description: One line under the pack name on its lobby tile. Says what playing it feels like, not what the rules are.

howToPlay.description: Optional prose for the rules page (src/ui/rules.js) — the things that cannot be derived from the declarations below: why the game is fun, or the one sentence that makes an unusual rule click. Everything factual (the deal, turn shape, card effects, what ends the match) is generated from the pack itself and must NOT be repeated here, or the two will drift. A string, or an array of paragraphs.

accent.description: The pack's colour on its lobby tile. A 6-digit hex literal and nothing else: this value reaches an inline style, and the UI re-validates it against the same pattern before use (§7b).

heroCards.description: The three faces fanned on the lobby tile. DISPLAY ONLY — these are drawn straight by src/ui/renderCard.js and are never looked up in the deck, so the lobby can render every tile from manifests alone without loading a single deck file. Choose faces that make the game recognisable at a glance.

rules.description: Template parameters; refined per-template by the allOf clauses below.

cardTags.description: Attach extra tags to cards by selector — the way to tag cards in built-in decks (Hearts tags its penalty cards). selector → tags to add.

flow.description: Overrides of the template's flow defaults (design doc §4): turn phases, round phases, order. Kept loose in v0; templates validate semantically.

zones.description: Additions to / overrides of the template's default zones.

announcements.description: Bespoke out-of-turn actions. Template conveniences (e.g. shedding's lastCardCall) generate their own announcements and do not need to be repeated here.

custom.description: Free-form bag intended for logic.js; the engine ignores it, and logic.js is UNWIRED, so nothing reads it today.

selector.description: Card selector: an exact card id ('spades-Q'), 'rank:<r>', 'suit:<s>', 'color:<c>', 'tag:<t>', or '*'. Where several selectors match one card, the most specific wins (exact id > tag/rank/suit/color > '*'); ties resolve to the last entry in the map. Selector keys must not contain dots (they appear in variant patch paths).

type.description: Built-in: skip, reverse, drawN, wild, wildDrawN, skipTarget, swapHands, rotateHands (src/engine/effects.js) — or a custom effect name exported by logic.js, which is UNWIRED; an unrecognised type is applied as no effect at all.

on.description: When the effect triggers. Milestones' Skip triggers on discard.

strategyOrHook.description: A template-provided strategy name, or 'hook:<fn>' referencing an export of the pack's logic.js. UNWIRED: nothing resolves a 'hook:' value today — see the note on the root description.

interactive.description: A zone with visibility:none that is still a control the player taps (a draw pile). Without it the table leaves invisible zones off the felt.

landing.description: Where a played and/or discarded card visibly lands when the move names no destination. Shared zones only; the first matching zone in definition order wins.

showsHeldValue.description: This pile's contents are worth points, so the felt shows what it has cost so far (Hearts' won pile).

when.description: 'zoneEmpty:<zone>' | 'zoneFull:<zone>'; '*' glob allowed in the zone id.

scoring.description: Round scoring and game-over live here (not in template rules). Effective card value = most specific cardValues match, else the card's deck-file value if non-null, else defaultValue, else 0.

cardValues.description: selector → points. null removes a value set by a broader selector.

oneOf.description: Numeric rank as value; non-numeric ranks fall through to 0.

bids.description: What a promise is worth, for the 'bids-and-bags' round score (src/engine/scoring.js). Read only by that strategy; a pack that does not bid has no business declaring it.

perTrick.description: Per trick of the contract, made — and the same number taken away when the side falls short.

overtrick.description: Per trick past the contract. Worth almost nothing now and a bag on the sheet, which is the point.

nil.description: For a bid of nothing, kept — and the same, negative, for taking a single trick.

blindNil.description: The same promise made blind. Defaults to twice `nil`.

bags.description: Overtricks accumulate per SIDE across the whole match and are paid for in lumps.

tricks.description: What taking tricks is worth beyond the cards in them, for the 'meld-and-tricks' round score (src/engine/scoring.js). The cards themselves are `cardValues`.

lastTrick.description: A bonus to whoever takes the final trick of the hand. Pinochle's ten is what turns 240 in card values into the 250 the deck is named for.

resolve.description: 'hook:<fn>' in logic.js. UNWIRED — see the note on the root description.

patch.description: Dotted-path → value applied over the manifest ('rules.drawWhenStuck': 'until-playable'). null deletes the key. Path segments split on '.'; selector keys therefore must not contain dots.

available.description: False for a variant the pack DECLARES but the template does not implement yet — kept as a statement of intent, but never offered in the new-game sheet, because a house rule you can switch on that changes nothing is worse than one that is not offered. Defaults to true.

back.description: Asset path for the card back.

faces.description: Asset path for a face sprite/SVG set; omit for the vanilla renderer.

table.description: Asset path for a table texture.

cardStyle.description: Which generated card art this pack uses (src/ui/cardStyles). Omit to let the registry infer: a standard-5x deck gets 'classic', a shedding template with its own deck gets 'shedding', anything else gets 'vanilla'. Declare it when the template does not describe the deck — Milestones is contract-rummy but wants 'sequencing' art, Stockpile is sequencing but wants 'rankrun'.

cardPalette.description: Card color name → hex. Keys are the deck's own `color` values (Wildfire: red/yellow/green/blue) or a style's named slots (rankrun: band1/band2/band3). Key ORDER is the order a wild's multi-color mark uses. Declaring this is also what makes a lobby tile match the table, since the lobby never loads a deck.

zoneOverlap.description: Zone id → how its visible cards are laid out: "horizontal" or "vertical" instead of a single stack, so every card shows its own value. PRESENTATION ONLY — it changes nothing about the rules, which is why it lives here and not in `zones`, and why a variant can flip it with a one-line patch ("ui.zoneOverlap.discard").

cardBack.description: The face-down side. Generated, not an asset — see `back` above for the asset form.

emblem.description: One or two characters in the center medallion. Omit for a plain pip.

matchOn.description: OR-matched against the active discard state. Cards with a wild effect are always playable.

effects.description: selector → effect; merged over (and overriding) effects declared in the deck file. The way to attach effects to built-in decks.

mustPlayIfAble.description: When true, drawing is illegal while you hold a card you could play. The rules page says which of the two games this is, and the validator enforces the same answer.

winner.description: DECLARATIVE ONLY. Win detection is fixed (first empty hand); this drives the wording on the rules page. Optional — omit it rather than declaring a value the template does not branch on.

lastCardCall.description: Generates a 'declare last card' announcement plus its missed-call challenge.

label.description: Player-facing announcement text (e.g. "Last card!"). Defaults to the id when absent.

followSuit.description: 'free' is no obligation at all; 'must' is the ordinary follow-suit rule; 'must-beat' is Pinochle's — follow the led suit AND play above the card that is currently winning if you hold one, and if you are void in it, trump, over-trumping whoever has already trumped when you can. Every narrowing relaxes to the wider pool when it would leave the seat with nothing to play.

leadConstraints.description: selector → constraint ('untilBroken'). Constraints relax automatically when they would leave a player with zero legal moves.

playConstraints.description: selector → constraint ('notTrick1'). Same relaxation rule as leadConstraints.

dealAdjust.description: player count → card ids removed from the deck so hands divide evenly.

trump.description: 'none' (the default, and what every no-trump pack says by omission), a suit the deck holds ('spades'), or 'chosen' — a round that names its own trump in the `trumpSuit` var. Declaring a trump suit does not on its own change who wins a trick: `trickWinner` says whether the resolution reads it.

trickWinner.description: How a trick resolves. 'highest-of-led' is the shape every pack shipped with: the highest card of the suit that was led, on the pack's own rank ladder. 'highest-trump-else-led' puts any card of the `trump` suit above every card of the led suit, however high.

dealAll.description: The whole deck goes out, and the pack is promising it divides evenly among every seat count it offers. Omit it and a deck that does not divide leaves its remainder undealt rather than giving one seat an extra card — at a trick game that is an extra trick. Hearts keeps its hands equal the other way, by removing cards (`dealAdjust`).

bidding.description: A sequential bidding phase before the first lead: each seat in turn, starting where the lead will, says what it will take. Its presence is what creates the phase; the scoring of what was promised is `scoring.roundScore` (see 'bids-and-bags' and 'meld-and-tricks').

unit.description: WHAT IS BEING PROMISED. 'tricks' is Spades: every seat bids once, every bid stands, and the side's contract is its two bids added up. 'points' is Pinochle's auction: a bid is a score the SIDE will reach, each seat must outbid whatever has already been said or pass (a bid of 0), and exactly one side ends up holding the contract — the highest bidder's. If everybody passes, the last seat to speak is stuck with `min`.

increment.description: The step between bids a seat may name. Pinochle raises in tens; a trick auction raises in ones.

namesTrump.description: The bid names a suit as well as a number, and the winning bid's suit becomes the round's trump (`trumpSuit`). Only meaningful beside `trump: "chosen"`.

min.description: The smallest bid. At a trick auction 0 is nil — a promise to take no trick at all; at a points auction 0 is a pass and `min` is the cheapest contract anybody may take.

oneOf.description: As many tricks as the seat holds cards, which is the most it could possibly take.

blindNil.description: A nil at double stakes, offered only to a side far enough behind. The platform models the wager and its entry condition; it cannot enforce the 'without looking' part, because the hand is dealt before any bid is possible.

behind.description: How far behind the leading side a side must be before its seats may bid blind.

melds.description:
A DECLARED MELD VOCABULARY, and the presence of it is what creates the `meld` phase between the auction and the first lead. A meld here is SCORED, not laid down: every seat commits a selection of cards from its hand at once (the same simultaneous-commit shape as a pass), the platform works out which of these it forms and for how much, and the cards stay in the hand to be played. Detection is src/templates/melds.js (`detectDeclaredMelds`); the table below is the pack's, and Pinochle's is the one it was written against.

A card may be counted in melds of DIFFERENT groups but never twice in the same one — the classic rule, and the reason the run and the royal marriage share the group 'marriage' while the pinochle and the arounds have their own.

label.description: What the felt calls it. Public: every seat is told what everybody melded.

group.description: Melds sharing a group compete for cards; melds in different groups may both use the same card. Omit for a meld that competes with nothing.

suits.description: How the suit of a card entry that does not name one is filled. 'named' — every entry says its own suit (a pinochle is the queen of SPADES with the jack of DIAMONDS). 'same' — one suit, any of them. 'same-not-trump' / 'trump' — the same, restricted (a marriage against a royal marriage). 'each' — the whole card list once per suit, which is what 'aces around' means.

cards.description: The cards the meld is made of, one entry per physical card — a double pinochle lists four. Three or more entries in ONE suit must be consecutive on the pack's `rankLadder`, or it is not a run and the detector refuses the declaration.

contracts.description: Ordered contracts; each is a list of items: set(n), run(n), colorGroup(n).

discardPickupForbidden.description: Selectors that may not be taken from the discard (Milestones' Skip).

meldForbidden.description: Selectors that may not be part of a meld at all (Milestones' Skip — an action you play at somebody, not a card with a place in a run). Same selector vocabulary as discardPickupForbidden.

buildRule.description: The closed rank range a build pile fills, ascending. Build-pile capacity is derived: to − from + 1. zoneFull fires when a pile completes.

buildStart.description: Selectors playable on an empty build pile.

playableFrom.description: Sources for plays onto build piles; stock and discard mean their top card only.

winner.description: DECLARATIVE ONLY. Win detection is fixed (first empty stock); this drives the wording on the rules page.

rules-climbing.description: The climbing genre (Thirteen, Big Two, President): play a SET of cards that beats the previous set of the same shape and size, or pass. Every table below is a declaration rather than a constant in src/templates/climbing.js — the combination vocabulary, the chopping ladder, whether a pass is final and which card opens the first hand are exactly what differs between the games of the genre.

deal.description: Cards per player, the same number at every seat count — the hand size is the name of the game and short-handed tables simply leave the remainder out of play (THIRTEEN_RULES.md D-11). A flat integer rather than `countOrByPlayers` for that reason.

combinations.description: What counts as a play, and NOTHING ELSE DOES. 'single', 'pair', 'triple' and 'quad' are fixed sizes; a variable-length shape names a FLOOR and must carry the '+' that says so ('run(3+)') — there is no such thing as a run of exactly five and nothing longer, so the schema does not let a pack write one. (A `bombs` shape below is the opposite and takes an exact size: a chopping ladder rung IS one specific shape.) A run's size is counted in CARDS and a strip of consecutive pairs' in PAIRS, which is also how `matchShape` and the `bombs` tokens below read them.

runExcludes.description: Cards no sequence may contain — Thirteen's 2, which sits at the TOP of the ladder and so has no neighbour above it ('K-A-2' is not a run and '2-2 A-A K-K' is not a bomb). Applies to runs and to consecutive pairs alike.

matchShape.description: How an answer must match what is on the table. 'same-type-same-size' is the genre's rule and the only one implemented: a five-card run is not a legal answer to a four-card run, it is simply not an answer (THIRTEEN_RULES.md D-7).

bombs.description: The OUT-OF-SHAPE ladder, low to high in declaration order. A bomb may be played on somebody else's turn-to-answer against a combination it does not match the shape of — which is what makes holding the highest card in the game something other than a free win. A bomb LED is an ordinary combination of its own shape and is answered in shape, so nothing here describes that case.

items.description: A shape, optionally narrowed by a card selector after a colon ('single:rank:2' is a lone 2; 'pair:rank:2' is a pair of them, and the selector must match EVERY card), or '*' for a bomb that chops anything.

passIsFinal.description: Once you have passed you are out of the trick and may not re-enter, even when the play comes back around below you. This is what makes the acting seats SHRINK as a trick goes on (`actingSeats`).

firstLead.description: Who opens hand one, and with what. Unlike trick-taking's `firstLead` this is an object, because the card names the LEADER and may also be required to be IN the combination they lead.

card.description: Card id ('spades-3'). Its holder leads the first hand of a match.

mustInclude.description: The opening combination must contain that card — the bare single, or it inside a pair, a run, anything legal.

laterLead.description: Who leads once hand one's opening is spent: 'trick-winner' is the last player to have played, both within a hand (when everybody else has passed the trick clears to them) and across one (the seat that went out leads the next deal).

direction.description: Which way the turn goes (`state.direction`). Counter-clockwise is the traditional Vietnamese direction and a real fact about the game, so the seat ring honours it.

winner.description: DECLARATIVE ONLY. Win detection is fixed (first empty hand); this drives the wording on the rules page.
